items.title: OpenAI's ring-shaped smart speaker will reportedly cost between $300 and $400
items.excerpt: OpenAI's first hardware device is a ring/doughnut-shaped, hockey-puck-sized screenless smart speaker designed with Jony Ive, priced at $300-$400. It is battery-powered and portable, with a camera and sensors feeding it context about its environment.

items.title: OpenAI's ChatGPT Speaker Will Be Hockey Puck-Sized and Cost Over $300
items.excerpt: OpenAI's doughnut-shaped ChatGPT speaker will use moving mechanical components to signal that it is responding and lights to show it is listening — an interaction model built around presence rather than a screen.

items.title: OpenAI's First Devices: Speaker, Smartphone, and More
items.excerpt: A roadmap roundup of OpenAI's hardware lineup: a portable AI smart speaker in early 2027, an 'AI agent phone' targeting mid-2027, and smart glasses further out — a device family where agents replace apps.

items.title: That AI wearable you don't like just got worse
items.excerpt: Friend's second-gen AI pendant adds a speaker and doubles the price to $249, keeping an always-on microphone and adding a $10/month subscription for memory retention beyond 30 days.

items.title: Meta Ray-Ban smart glasses are getting smarter with a significant AI model upgrade
items.excerpt: Meta's v127 update brings the Muse Spark model to Ray-Ban Display, plus Neural Handwriting — writing prompts with a finger on any flat surface via the Neural Band — and Threads/Instagram voice interactions.

items.title: The Company Behind Ugly Gold Phones Is Now Making Ugly Gold Smart Glasses
items.excerpt: Luxury customizer Caviar unveiled 'Odyssey,' a $6,840 24-karat gold-plated Ray-Ban Meta AI glasses limited to 24 pieces — AI eyewear treated as a fashion object rather than a gadget.

items.title: Viture's New XR Glasses Are Sharper, Brighter, and Way Less Expensive
items.excerpt: Viture's Pro 2 XR glasses drop to $299 while getting sharper, brighter and roughly 20% lighter than the previous generation — pushing wearable displays toward everyday price and comfort.

items.title: The Viral 'Antizuck' App Makes Spotting Smart Glasses Easy (and Potentially Pointless)
items.excerpt: A $3 iOS app uses Bluetooth signatures to detect nearby camera-equipped smart glasses, an emerging counter-design response to always-on AI eyewear in public space.

items.title: Another huge Pixel Watch 5 leak showcases everything from design to health features
items.excerpt: Leaked marketing materials show the Pixel Watch 5 leading with 'Ask Gemini' plus Fitbit's Personal Health Coach, heart-health, sleep, SpO2 and cardio-load tracking ahead of the August 12 launch.

items.title: Pixel Watch 5 specs leak reveals what's new: 'Accelerated' chip, 2nd-gen Active Band, more
items.excerpt: The Pixel Watch 5 is said to move to a Snapdragon W5 Gen 2 'Accelerated' chip with more RAM and 64GB storage — headroom aimed squarely at on-device Gemini experiences on the wrist.

items.title: I hope Galaxy Z Flip 8 isn't the last of its kind, but I can see why it might
items.excerpt: The Z Flip 8's redesigned FlexWindow brings Gemini Intelligence and Now Brief to the cover screen, but app restrictions limit how far the glanceable, unfold-free AI interaction model actually goes.

items.title: iOS 27 basically turns your iPhone and AirPods into an Apple Watch at the gym
items.excerpt: iOS 27 extends GymKit beyond the Apple Watch, letting iPhone plus AirPods Pro 3 tap gym equipment for real-time metrics — sensing moves off the wrist and into the ears.

items.title: Two new affordable smartwatches launch with aluminum alloy cases
items.excerpt: Rollme launched the AI Watch 2 and AI Watch 3 at $39.99 each, bundling AI chat access and WhatsApp/Telegram quick replies — AI assistants arriving at the bottom of the wearable price ladder.

items.title: Asus releases Chromebook CX15 bundle with Google AI Pro and 5 TB cloud storage
items.excerpt: Asus is now selling the Chromebook CX15 with a three-month Google AI Pro membership including Gemini Advanced and 5TB of storage — AI subscriptions becoming part of the hardware spec sheet.
